focus: auto-heal batch pipeline: live dashboard acquisition, hard 1st-party filtering, pre-fix visualization, no-approval fixes, MR-per-error, attribution registry
sample_prompts: summarize the highest-risk recurring Dynatrace frontend errors
investigate this Safari undefined-property crash and produce a reviewer-grade fix summary
run auto-heal on my-app-prod and show the remediation rate
batch fix Dynatrace errors for my-web-frontend

heal_mode_expected_behavior: before touching Dynatrace, resolves --frontend and --first-party-domain (asking if either isn't given) and confirms Chrome tenant access — there is no CSV or token alternative to choose between
no human approval prompt for eligible high-confidence fixes; only allowed stops are a dirty git tree and the Phase -1 acquisition setup

1st-party is a HARD filter (extraction-time domain/vendor check, then evidence-stage stack check) — 3rd-party errors never enter the fix queue on a 'suspected' basis, but are still shown excluded on the visualization
only errors with >=100 affected users AND confirmed 1st-party enter the fix queue, over a 7-day rolling window
renders a pre-fix triage board (Artifact) showing every candidate's planned action before any code changes, plus excluded/skipped rows
each fix branch is cut from freshly fetched origin/master (verified via merge-base) and produces exactly one MR
test gate before every MR: reproducing spec + eslint + targeted ChromeHeadlessCI run; retry once then downgrade to reported
low-confidence errors get a triage writeup in the registry, no branch, no MR
run ends with the registry finalized, the visualization redeployed showing fixed/not-fixed, and a report showing remediation rate vs the 75% target
